title: A Song of Ice and Fire
description: Series of novels by George R. R. Martin
wiki_lead:
A Song of Ice and Fire is a series of high fantasy novels by the American author George R. R. Martin. Martin began writing the first volume, A Game of Thrones, in 1991, and published it in 1996. Martin, who originally envisioned the series as a trilogy, has released five out of seven planned volumes. The most recent entry in the series, A Dance with Dragons, was published in 2011. Since then, Martin claims to have been working on the sixth novel, titled The Winds of Winter. A seventh novel, A Dream of Spring, is planned to follow.
A Song of Ice and Fire depicts a violent world dominated by political realism. What little supernatural power exists is confined to the margins of the known world. Moral ambiguity pervades the books, and many of the storylines frequently raise questions concerning loyalty, pride, human sexuality, piety, and the morality of violence. The story unfolds through an alternating set of subjective points of view, the success or survival of any of which is never assured. Each chapter is told from a limited third-person perspective, drawn from a group of characters that expands from nine in the first novel to thirty-one by the fifth.
The novels are set on the fictional continents of Westeros and Essos (the world as a whole does not have an established name). Martin's stated inspirations for the series include many supposed historic events. The work as a whole consists of three interwoven plots: a dynastic war among several families for control of Westeros, the ambition of the surviving members of the dethroned Targaryen dynasty to return from their exile in Essos and reassume the Iron Throne, and the growing threat posed by the powerful supernatural Others from the northernmost region of Westeros.
As of 2026, more than 100 million copies in 47 languages had been sold. The fourth and fifth volumes reached the top of the New York Times Best Seller lists when published in 2005 and 2011, respectively. Among the many derived works are several prequel novellas, three television series, a comic book adaptation, and several card, board, and video games. The series has received critical acclaim for its world-building, characters, and narrative.

Plot synopsis

A Song of Ice and Fire takes place in a fictional world in which seasons often last for years and can end unpredictably. Before the events of the first novel, the Seven Kingdoms of Westeros were united under the Targaryen dynasty, establishing military supremacy through their control of dragons. The Targaryens ruled for nearly three hundred years, continuing beyond the extinction of the dragons. Their dynasty eventually ended with a rebellion led by Lord Robert Baratheon, in which Aerys II "the Mad King" Targaryen was killed, and Robert was proclaimed king of the Seven Kingdoms. At the beginning of A Game of Thrones, 15 years have passed since Robert's rebellion, with a nine-year-long summer nearing its end.

grok_lead: A Song of Ice and Fire is an epic fantasy series of novels written by American author George R. R. Martin, comprising a tale of noble families vying for power in the medieval-inspired world of Westeros through intricate political machinations, brutal wars, and emerging supernatural threats including dragons and ancient ice creatures from beyond the northern Wall. The series blends elements of high fantasy with gritty realism, drawing comparisons to historical fiction for its morally ambiguous characters and focus on themes of power, betrayal, and survival. The saga was initially conceived as a trilogy but expanded to a planned seven volumes due to the expansive narrative. As of February 2026, five novels have been published: A Game of Thrones (1996), A Clash of Kings (1998), A Storm of Swords (2000), A Feast for Crows (2005), and A Dance with Dragons (2011). No new mainline novel has been released since A Dance with Dragons (2011). The Winds of Winter remains unfinished, with Martin reporting approximately 1,100 pages written in a January 2026 interview and expressing hope to complete it soon by prioritizing it over other commitments, though no release date exists. Recent focus has been on adaptations, including HBO's A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms (Season 1 concluded, Season 2 filming), House of the Dragon Season 3 (teaser released, June 2026 premiere), and a Royal Shakespeare Company stage play Game of Thrones: The Mad King (summer 2026 premiere). Set primarily on the continent of Westerosâa landmass roughly the size of South America divided into the Seven Kingdoms ruled from the capital of King's Landingâthe story unfolds against a backdrop of long summers and harsh winters that can last years, symbolizing cycles of prosperity and peril. Across the Narrow Sea lies Essos, a vast eastern continent featuring nomadic tribes, slave cities, and the exiled Targaryen dynasty seeking to reclaim their ancestral throne with the aid of newly hatched dragons. Central to the plot is the Iron Throne, a twisted monstrosity of jagged blades forged from the swords of Aegon the Conqueror's enemies, around which houses like Stark, Lannister, Baratheon, and Targaryen clash in a web of alliances, assassinations, and battles. The series has garnered critical acclaim for its complex characters, intricate world-building, and unflinching depiction of violence and human frailty, earning Martin the moniker "the American Tolkien" from Time magazine. It achieved massive commercial success, with over 90 million copies sold worldwide by 2015, and inspired spin-off works including the companion history The World of Ice & Fire (2014). The novels served as the basis for HBO's Emmy-winning television series Game of Thrones (2011â2019), which dramatized the early books and significantly boosted the franchise's global popularity, though later seasons diverged from the source material.
